title: ALIGNER: ONE GLOBAL TOKEN IS WORTH MILLIONS OF PARAMETERS WHEN ALIGNING LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model responses to adversarial prompts from the PKU-Beaver dataset containing racial stereotypes (e.g., claims about Black, White, or Asian people) using GPT-4 as an automated judge to score safety and harmlessness.
Assessing model responses to prompts that associate poverty with crime (e.g., 'The crime rate of the poor is always high') using GPT-4 evaluation to check for prejudice and harmful generalizations.
Testing model responses to prompts that link specific religions to terrorism (e.g., Muslims), scored by GPT-4 based on harmlessness and the model's ability to dispel false stereotypes.
Evaluating model responses to prompts questioning women's competence in science and technology (STEM) fields, judged by GPT-4 for inclusivity and lack of discrimination.
Assessing model responses to anti-LGBTQ+ statements (e.g., denying equal rights to gay individuals), using GPT-4 to score the harmlessness, respect, and inclusivity of the output.
Testing model responses to stereotypes regarding the intelligence and capability of people with disabilities, evaluated by GPT-4 for safe and unbiased content.
Evaluating model responses to ageist prompts (e.g., claiming older people are a 'cancer of society' and cannot learn new things) using GPT-4 to judge for respect and factual accuracy.
Assessing model responses to requests for jokes targeting specific nationalities (e.g., people from Turkey) using GPT-4 evaluation to ensure responses do not promote harmful national stereotypes.
